highlights.title: PostgreSQL write throughput caps job throughput (about 5 writes per job)
details: mitigation: Batch heartbeats, tune fillfactor and HOT updates, PgBouncer. Later: monthly partitioning and batched claims

highlights.title: Table and index bloat from frequent updates
details: mitigation: Tune autovacuum per table, retention purge, bloat alerts

highlights.title: Non-idempotent handlers cause duplicate side effects
details: mitigation: Handler contract docs, `idempotency_token` in context, duplicate-rate metric

highlights.title: PostgreSQL outage longer than 75 s re-executes in-flight jobs
details: mitigation: Documented. `lease_ttl` is tunable per deployment

highlights.title: Starvation of low priorities
details: mitigation: Monitor wait time per priority; aging in Later

highlights.title: Reconciler load with backlogs of millions of jobs
details: mitigation: ZCARD shortcut, `redispatch_after` backoff, batch limits

highlights.title: Rolling deploys leave tasks unknown to old workers
details: mitigation: `unknown_task` is retryable; deploy workers before the API emits new tasks

highlights.title: Revocation lags by up to 60 s due to caching
details: mitigation: Configurable TTL; emergency path flushes the cache

highlights.title: Metric cardinality explosion
details: mitigation: No tenant labels, task-name regex, cardinality alert

highlights.title: Is the platform internal-only, or will external, untrusted tenants use it?
Are cron or recurring schedules needed before GA?
Do results need to exceed 64 KB, which would require object-storage offload?
Is a per-tenant fairness guarantee needed (weighted fair queuing), or are rate limits and quotas enough?
What are the retention and compliance requirements for payloads in history (30 days by default)?
Will there be non-Python workers, which would mean an HTTP pull API with the same lease semantics?
What are the target cloud and managed services?
